world_set.source: R19 frozen prospective holdout worlds R19-W01 through R19-W08
world_set.reason: Compare the four R19 exact-PASS worlds against the four R19 candidate-resource-OPEN worlds using only CNF graph structure already frozen before R19 execution.

primal_graph_contract.vertices: all variables present in the frozen frame CNF
primal_graph_contract.edges: undirected edge {u,v} iff u and v co-occur in at least one frozen frame clause
primal_graph_contract.bridge_variables: R19 frozen bridge set; never eliminated during R23 heuristic replay
primal_graph_contract.internal_variables: all frame variables not in bridge set
primal_graph_contract.component_view: remove bridge vertices, compute connected components on the internal-induced graph, and for each internal component report the set of adjacent bridge variables

frozen_elimination_heuristics.rule: At each step among remaining internal variables choose the variable with the fewest missing edges among its current neighbors; ties by current degree, then original frame literal-occurrence count descending, then numeric variable id ascending. Add all missing edges among its current neighbors before removing it. Bridge variables participate as neighbors but are never selected.

At each step among remaining internal variables choose the variable with smallest current degree; ties by missing-fill-edge count, then original frame literal-occurrence count descending, then numeric variable id ascending. Add all missing edges among its current neighbors before removing it. Bridge variables participate as neighbors but are never selected.

local_table_feasibility_landmarks.separator_width_16: At most 2^16 = 65,536 assignments over an induced separator neighborhood. This is a descriptive engineering landmark, not a complexity theorem.
local_table_feasibility_landmarks.separator_width_20: At most 2^20 = 1,048,576 assignments over an induced separator neighborhood. This is a secondary caution landmark.
local_table_feasibility_landmarks.interpretation_rule: A heuristic width above a landmark is evidence only about that frozen heuristic order, not a lower bound on treewidth or proof that no better decomposition exists.

compare: minimum of the two heuristic induced widths per world
group_comparison.purpose: Determine whether the R19 OPEN frontier coincides with visibly larger structural separator burden under two fixed truth-blind heuristics and whether component factoring is structurally plausible before implementing a new semantic representation.

verdict_rules.component_promising: R19-W05 has at least 2 internal components after bridge removal AND largest_internal_component_size <= 32 AND largest_component_bridge_boundary_size <= 16.
verdict_rules.low_width_promising: If component_promising is false, R19-W05 minimum induced width across the two frozen heuristics <= 16.
verdict_rules.still_wide: If neither promising rule holds and R19-W05 minimum induced width across the two heuristics > 20.

next_action_rule: Only after R23 preserves the structural result may a new decomposition-based semantic representation be specified. R23 itself may not claim that a heuristic induced width is optimal treewidth or that decomposition solves SAT efficiently.
claim_ceiling: Graph-structural evidence on eight finite frozen worlds only. No exact treewidth theorem, no lower bound for all decompositions, no unseen semantic evidence beyond already-sealed R19, no SAT-in-P, P=NP, or P!=NP conclusion.
